definition: Italian term for a female street sex worker who solicits clients by walking public streets.
notes: Derived from passeggiare (to walk); the standard Italian designation for a streetwalking sex worker; not highly crude due to its descriptive, euphemistic form.

definition: Italian slang for a sex worker who is contacted by telephone; a call girl.
notes: Literally means ring or buzz (as of a telephone); the term foregrounds the telephone-solicitation model of indoor sex work; widely known and used in journalism.

definition: English loanword used in Italian for a high-end sex worker who accompanies clients socially as well as sexually.
notes: The English origin softens explicitness; widely used in Italian press and legal discourse as a euphemism for a paid sexual companion.

definition: English loanword used in Italian for a sex worker hired by telephone or through an agency.
notes: Less common than squillo or escort in contemporary Italian; found primarily in journalistic and translated contexts; retains its English form unchanged.

definition: Roman dialect crude slang for a pimp; a man who lives off and controls a sex worker's earnings.
notes: Originates in Romanesco dialect; now broadly understood nationally but retains a distinctly Roman flavor and is considered highly offensive.

definition: Archaic and legal Italian term for a pimp or exploiter of prostitution, derived from Latin leno.
notes: Directly from Latin leno; survives in Italian Penal Code language (reato di lenocinio) for the offense of exploiting or facilitating prostitution; rarely used in everyday speech.

definition: Historical Italian term for a procurer or go-between who arranged clients for sex workers; in modern usage it primarily means sycophant or toady.
notes: The sex-work meaning is archaic; the dominant modern sense is flatterer or toady; the procurer meaning is preserved in Commedia dell'Arte tradition where il Ruffiano is a stock character type.

definition: Italian euphemism for a pimp; literally protector, framing the exploitative role as one of provision and care.
notes: The euphemistic framing inverts the actual dynamic of exploitation; used in court testimony and journalism when directly naming the relationship without the crude connotations of magnaccia.

definition: Italian word for a brothel; the same word was borrowed directly into English.
notes: The Italian word bordello was loaned into English; in modern Italian it is somewhat dated but universally understood; less clinical than postribolo, less crude than casino in the brothel sense.

definition: Italian word (stress on first syllable, no accent) for a brothel; in contemporary usage the same word overwhelmingly means mess or chaos.
notes: Distinct from casinò (gambling establishment, final-syllable stress); the brothel meaning is archaic but survives in the colloquial exclamation che casino (what a mess), which retains the connotation of disorder originally associated with brothels.

definition: Literary and formal Italian word for a brothel, used in journalism, historical writing, and anti-prostitution legal discourse.
notes: More formal and neutral than bordello; preferred in institutional and legislative texts discussing Italian prostitution policy, especially coverage of the Merlin Law.

definition: Historical Italian term for a state-licensed and regulated brothel that operated legally before the Merlin Law of 1958 abolished regulated prostitution in Italy.
notes: Literally closed house; the shuttered windows preserved client anonymity; the Merlin Law (Legge Merlin, 1958) closed all case chiuse, making this term historically bounded; still widely recognized through historical and political debate about re-legalizing regulated prostitution.

definition: Classical and literary Italian term for a brothel, derived from Latin lupa (she-wolf), which was Roman argot for a prostitute.
notes: The famous Pompeii brothel excavated in the 1st century CE is called the Lupanare; encountered mainly in classical studies, archaeology, and literary contexts; very low general recognition.

definition: The standard Italian word for pornography; printed, visual, or digital material depicting sexual acts intended to cause arousal.
Italian compound noun for a pornographic film.
notes: Typically written as one word or hyphenated; widely used in journalistic and colloquial contexts.

definition: Italian compound for a male pornographic film star; a man who performs in pornography as a named and recognized performer.
notes: Compound of porno and divo (idol or male star); the divo component implies celebrity status within the adult industry, distinguishing a recognized performer from an anonymous one.

definition: Italian compound for a female pornographic film star; a woman who performs in pornography as a named and recognized performer.
notes: Compound of porno and diva (goddess or female star); the diva component carries connotations of glamour and celebrity; slightly more widely recognized than pornodivo, likely due to broader press coverage of female performers.

definition: Italian compound for a male actor who performs in pornographic films.
notes: More neutral than pornodivo; attore (actor) frames the role as a professional performance occupation rather than stardom; preferred in legal and journalistic contexts.

definition: Italian compound for a female actress who performs in pornographic films.
notes: More neutral and more frequently encountered than pornodiva in journalism and legal texts; attrice (actress) normalizes the role as a professional occupation.

definition: Italian word for an orgy; a sexual gathering involving multiple participants engaging with each other simultaneously.
notes: Retains the secondary historical sense of ritual excess in ancient Greco-Roman religious rites (from Greek orgia); the modern sexual sense is overwhelmingly dominant in contemporary usage.

definition: Italian term for the lifestyle practice of consensual partner-swapping or swinging among couples.
notes: Derived from scambiare (to exchange or swap); the standard Italian term for the swinger lifestyle; used in community self-identification and in sociological and journalistic coverage of the practice.

definition: Archaic and literary Italian word for the prostitution trade as an institution or industry.
notes: From Latin meretrix (prostitute); appears in legal and historical texts, particularly in debate over the Legge Merlin; rarely encountered in everyday speech; the related verb meretriciare is virtually extinct.

definition: Italian phrase for sex tourism; travel undertaken primarily to engage with sex workers, typically exploiting economic disparities.
notes: Standard journalistic and legal terminology; appears in Italian criminal code provisions addressing international sexual exploitation and child sex tourism; two-word noun phrase, never contracted to a single compound.

definition: The standard everyday Italian word for a condom; a latex sheath worn on the penis during sex to prevent pregnancy and STI transmission.
notes: Cognate with French préservatif and Spanish preservativo; the default term in public health campaigns, pharmacy contexts, and everyday speech; neither crude nor strongly clinical.

definition: The clinical and formal Italian term for a condom, derived from profilassi (prophylaxis) and emphasizing the disease-prevention function.
notes: Preferred in medical literature, pharmacological labeling, and institutional public health communication; the English cognate prophylactic occupies the same register; less common in casual speech than preservativo.
